subject: Inference throughput & latency benchmarking — test plan and results
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@globex.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmarking questionnaire: inference throughput & latency for RFP

Hannah,

Thanks for engaging — as part of our RFP evaluation we need a detailed, reproducible benchmarking package showing how Redwood performs across the following dimensions. I've attached a short PDF with the questionnaire, but important items below: 

- Required metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (in ms), throughput (tokens/sec, requests/sec), GPU utilization, CPU utilization, memory and KV cache hit rates. 
- Workloads: 3 sequence length profiles: short (32 tokens), mid (128), long (1024). Provide separate results for each. 
- Models and variants to test: your recommended open LLMs plus a 7B and 13B quantized variant; clarify quantization scheme and exact model hashes.
- Deployments: results for hosted API, Dedicated (reserved pool), and Private (VPC) if available. If full Private can't be executed, describe differences and provide extrapolated numbers with methodology.
- Concurrency and scaling: tests at 1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent clients; include warm and cold start behavior and auto-scale ramp time.
- Batching and KV cache: show performance with batching disabled and with your recommended batching config; show behavior for cached prefixes vs uncached.
- Reproducibility: provide test harness, command lines, seed text, synthetic dataset sample, raw per-request logs (timestamps + request id), and the environment (GPU model, CUDA/cuDNN versions, driver).
- Percentiles: show how p99 changes with concurrency and sequence length; provide plots or CSV.
- Clarifications: if there are any constraints (e.g., GPU models not available in hosted tier), call them out.

We need the package by end of day 2026-03-11 to finalize vendor scoring. Can you confirm receipt and give a proposed test plan/timeline?

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Senior Sourcing Manager
Globex Corporation

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@globex.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-09T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking questionnaire: inference throughput & latency for RFP

Laura — thanks, received. We're prepared to run a focused reproducible benchmark set that matches your questionnaire. High-level proposed plan: 

1) Scope and baseline: run 3 sequence-length profiles (32/128/1024) on the following model variants: Llama2-13B (fp16), Llama2-13B (4-bit quant / q4_k_m), and a 7B quant variant. We'll include model hashes and the Docker images we used.

2) Environments: hosted API (standard), Dedicated reserved pool (A100-80GB equivalent), and a private-replicated container on a customer-similar VPC node (NVIDIA H100 where available). If we cannot reproduce an exact Private environment on your side within timeline, we'll provide an annotated extrapolation using kernel-level metrics.

3) Concurrency matrix: 1, 8, 32, 128 parallel clients, each issuing streaming token requests. For each concurrency point we will run 10k requests for short/mid and 2k for long sequences to keep test time reasonable.

4) Warm vs cold: measure initial cold-start (first request after model load), then steady-state and after a 30-minute idle period to simulate cache eviction.

5) Batching / KV cache: tests with batching disabled and with our production batching profile (max batch 128, dynamic batch window 20ms). We'll show per-token latency and tokens/sec. KV cache hit-rate analysis included.

6) Artifacts: CSV with per-request latencies and request ids, aggregated percentiles, Grafana screenshots, kernel-level metrics JSON, and a short write-up describing methodology and any caveats.

We can complete a preliminary package by EoD 2026-03-10 PST and provide a final reproducible artifacts set by midday 2026-03-11 PST. Attaching our test plan and will push results as CSV plus kernel metrics.

Would you like us to prioritize any particular model variant or hardware profile?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_benchmark_test_plan_20260310.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-09T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: test execution notes

Looping in details for the run:
- I'll reserve a Dedicated pool (4x A100-80GB) for a 4 hr window on 2026-03-10 02:00-06:00 UTC to run the matrix; will push images to the reserved nodes and pin kernels.
- Aditya: can you enable kernel-level tracing (nvprof / Nsight stats) + perf samples and prepare the script that emits per-token timestamps and request_id in JSONL? We need exact matching request ids for p99 attribution.
- We'll capture cold starts by cycling the model process between runs. Also prepare the batching harness with adjustable windows.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@globex.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: 2026-03-10T08:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking questionnaire: inference throughput & latency for RFP

Thanks for the plan — two quick clarifications before you run: 

1) For long sequences (1024), please include a control where attention caching is disabled (simulate independent short prompts appended to form long sequences) so we can see worst-case memory and compute.
2) For p99 numbers, please provide both raw p99 and a p99-excluding-outliers computed by trimming the single worst 0.1% to account for infra noise. Label both.
3) For the Private extrapolation, list clearly which micro-ops / kernel optimizations you assume when mapping from A100 to H100 (if you extrapolate).

If you can include those items in the preliminary run that would be ideal.

Laura

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@globex.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-11T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking questionnaire: inference throughput & latency for RFP — results and next steps

Laura — attached are the preliminary artifacts from the Dedicated run (A100 pool) executed 2026-03-10 UTC. Highlights below and attachments include the full CSVs and kernel metrics JSON.

Summary highlights (Dedicated, Llama2-13B q4_k_m, batching=dynamic):
- Short (32 tokens): p50=18ms, p90=28ms, p95=35ms, p99=62ms; throughput ~1,200 requests/sec (single model replica under 8 concurrent clients).
- Mid (128 tokens): p50=65ms, p90=120ms, p95=170ms, p99=330ms; throughput ~480 requests/sec.
- Long (1024 tokens, KV cache enabled): p50=540ms, p90=780ms, p95=980ms, p99=1,600ms; tokens/sec drops as expected due to quadratic attention. 
- Long sequence control (cache disabled, independent segments): p99 observed spikes up to 4,300ms on A100 under 32 concurrent clients — included as "control_long_no_cache.csv".
- Cold starts: first-request latencies vary by model load time (~4-9s depending on quantization), included in cold_start.csv.
- Kernel metrics: we included GPU utilization and per-op breakdown. For H100 extrapolation we documented likely improvements from TensorFloat32 and improved matmul kernel throughput; we conservatively model a 1.3x tokens/sec improvement for long sequences in the extrapolation doc.

Artifacts attached: redwood_benchmark_results_20260310.csv, redwood_kernel_metrics_20260310.json, control_long_no_cache.csv, redwood_benchmark_test_plan_20260310.pdf. The CSVs have request_id and per-request timestamps for full reproducibility.

Next steps: we can run the hosted API profile if you want numbers from our multi-tenant environment (note: exact GPU may vary) and schedule a live demo to walk through the graphs and kernel traces. Would you like us to prioritize hosted numbers or proceed to a Private on-site test? We can also produce the p99-trimmed numbers you requested (p99 excluding worst 0.1%) by EoD PST.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_results_20260310.csv, redwood_kernel_metrics_20260310.json, control_long_no_cache.csv
